target_objects: control/{ingest,parse,report}/*.json ledgers and control/locks/*.lock (new, outside the parity surface)
golden_baseline_location: The legacy scripts themselves, executed by etl/legacy-extra/parity/harness.py on the same fresh estate root as the candidate (cases dev, qa, edges, empty).

acceptance_checks.description: After the chain runs, the drop directory is empty and incoming/ holds the same .done files byte for byte as the legacy chain leaves.
parsed/*.psv is byte-identical to the sed|cut|paste|awk output, including trailing-space trimming, implied decimals and the awk numeric coercion of non-numeric amounts.
finance_billing_*.csv and .xls are byte-identical to the Perl report on every harness case, including UNKNOWN(rt) labels and bytewise key ordering.
Running the chain a second time on the same estate changes no file outside control/.
The parse ledger records the TRL count against the body record count for every file and flags a mismatch; --strict quarantines the file instead of reporting from it.
Every body record is typed (date, decimal amount, currency, record type) and invalid records are attributed by line number and reason in the ledger.
Overlapping runs of the same stage or the chain are refused via flock (exit 3), never run twice.
Any stage failure exits non-zero with a traceback; no output is redirected to /dev/null.
.github/workflows/custbill-parity-nightly.yml reruns the parity table every night and opens or updates a drift issue on failure.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: latin-1 (every byte is one character; the legacy chain runs in LC_ALL=C)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Input bytes are copied through to .psv and .csv unchanged; CR is content, a trailing newline does not create an empty record, an unterminated last line still counts.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: There are no invalid bytes under latin-1; nothing is re-encoded.

malformed_record_policy.details: Default mode reproduces the legacy output exactly (short lines yield empty columns, non-numeric amounts become 0.00) and attributes each problem in control/parse/latest.json. --strict (CUSTBILL_STRICT=1) quarantines the file and fails the run.

empty_input_semantics.details: No drop files: ingest and parse are no-ops and the report stage writes the header-only CSV/XLS, as the legacy chain does. A header-only .dat produces a zero-byte .psv.

planted_anomalies.description: CUSTBILL_EDGES.dat declares TRL count 99 against 4 body records; legacy only logs it.
Record type 99 in CUSTBILL_EDGES.dat; legacy renders it as UNKNOWN(99).
The .xls artifact is a byte copy of the CSV, not a workbook. Parity pins the bytes, so the Spark job reproduces it.
planted_anomalies.reason: Finance accepts the cutover only on byte-identical reports; a real workbook is a post-cutover change recorded in etl/custbill-spark/README.md.

planted_anomalies.description: Non-numeric amounts silently become 0.00 in the .psv.
